seoTitle: How to Fix ChatGPT 'Too Many Concurrent Requests'
metaDescription: Fix the ChatGPT 'Too Many Concurrent Requests' error with simple browser and account fixes on both web and mobile.
intro: Seeing the 'Too Many Concurrent Requests' error in ChatGPT usually means multiple requests are hitting the server or your session at once. This guide walks through the common fixes for this error on both the ChatGPT website and mobile app.

steps.heading: Close duplicate tabs or sessions
steps.body: Check if you have ChatGPT open in multiple browser tabs or devices at once, since this can trigger overlapping requests.

steps.heading: Clear your browser cache
steps.body: Clear cached data and cookies for the ChatGPT site, then reload the page to start with a clean session.

steps.heading: Refresh and re-login
steps.body: Log out of ChatGPT, refresh the page, and log back in to reset your session.

steps.heading: Check OpenAI server status
steps.body: Visit OpenAI's status page to confirm the issue isn't a wider server-side problem outside of your control.

steps.heading: Try the mobile app or a different browser
steps.body: If the error persists on web, try the ChatGPT mobile app or switch browsers to rule out a local issue.

faq.question: Does this error mean my account is banned?
faq.answer: No, 'Too Many Concurrent Requests' is a technical rate-limiting message, not an indication of an account restriction.

faq.question: Can having multiple tabs open cause this error?
faq.answer: Yes, running ChatGPT in several tabs or devices simultaneously can trigger this error since multiple requests overlap.

faq.question: Will clearing cache delete my chat history?
faq.answer: No, clearing your browser cache doesn't delete your ChatGPT conversation history, which is stored on OpenAI's servers.

faq.question: How do I know if it's an OpenAI server issue instead of my device?
faq.answer: Check OpenAI's official status page — if it shows ongoing incidents, the error is likely server-side rather than caused by your setup.
